properties.instruction:
A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 100 AM CDT for north central
Minnesota.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Although a
tornado is not immediately likely, if one is spotted, act quickly and
move to a place of safety inside a sturdy structure such as a
basement or small interior room.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued July 24 at 9:04PM MST until July 24 at 10:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ

FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1045 PM MST.

* At 904 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.8 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.2 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southwestern Cochise County.

This includes the following highways...
Route 90 between mile markers 329 and 336. Route 80 between mile
markers 325 and 335.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Davis Rd between HWY 80 & HWY 191.

Davis road from Highway 80 to Frontier Road is closed due to
flooding. There are likely other areas seeing flooding this evening.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 4:56PM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Monday July 27.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 24 at 2:51PM AKDT until July 24 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by prior excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Kroto Creek and Moose Creek near Oilwell Road.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 248 PM AKDT, river gauge report for Moose Creek at Oilwell
Road indicates that water levels are falling but still remain
above flood stage this afternoon. Minor flooding is
occurring, especially near Kroto Creek and Moose Creek.

- Rainfall has moved out of the advisory area, allowing water
levels to begin receding.  However, drainage from prior heavy
rainfall will continue to cause flooding through Friday
night.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 23 at 1:44PM AKDT until July 25 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water could enter a few low-lying cabins along the Yentna River,
particularly near Lake Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 139 PM AKDT, recent heavy rains have caused rapid river
rises. Minor flooding is expected to continue, especially
along the Yentna River near Lake Creek.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 1:30pm the stage was 21.5 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.

At 22.0 feet: Several lodges and resorts will have water in a
number of cabins with water also encroaching the main lodge
buildings.





- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- If you live near or along Yentna River, stay alert and be
prepared to take action.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
